correctness.rationale: For any of the three complex smooth-conic baskets, tau=3k(k-1)-1 follows from local A1 and A3 Tjurina numbers. The Dimca–Sernesi bound r>=ceil((3/4)(2k)-2), and the du Plessis–Wall two-sided bounds eliminate every other integer r: k=2 tau5 excludes r1 by lower bound6 and r3 by upper bound3; k=3 tau17 excludes r>=4 by upper bound at r4=15; k=4 tau35 excludes r>=5 by upper bound at r5=33. For r=k=d/2 the Dimca–Sticlaru minimal plus-one criterion holds tau+2=r^2-r(d-1)+(d-1)^2. These steps are parameter-independent. The standalone verification script checks all possible integer r values; it does not purport to prove the cited general bounds.

originality.rationale: The closest original source, Măcinic–Pokora Theorem 3.1, computes one representative per basket after exhibiting parametric realization families. The 2026 Bromboszcz–Jarosławski–Pokora Theorem 4.2 assumes plus-one generation to obtain necessary baskets and establishes realizability with examples, not sufficiency for every member. Its Proposition 4.3 proves parameter-uniform homology for the different basket of four nodes and ten tacnodes. The 2022 Dimca–Janasz–Pokora classification of nearly-free conics concerns the zero-node boundary. The two-sided inequality argument yields a statement of universal Betti-rigidity not implied by existence or conditional necessity; all named sources were materially inspected and the indexed overlap searches were performed. Residual risk: an unindexed earlier reformulation of this short consequence of standard inequalities.
residual_risks: A differently worded prior conclusion or undocumented folklore may apply the same classical inequalities to all realizations of these baskets.
The numerical inequalities and characterization are established results; originality rests entirely on the universal application to this natural high-tangency stratum.
The claim concerns graded minimal resolution invariants, not explicit generator coefficients, and excludes other baskets.

value.rationale: The three baskets are precisely the near-maximal tangency and exactly-two-node cases singled out for geometric realization in published conic arrangements. Determining the entire minimal Jacobian syzygy-degree pattern for all realizations (rather than computing one instance or giving necessary conditions) is a complete natural homological rigidity classification. The no-weak-Ziegler-pair consequence is of direct interest given published strong Ziegler phenomena in related conic-line strata. The combination of deep Tjurina bounds and local Arnold-exponent bounds leaves zero freedom for a homological jump. It does not extrapolate to other baskets and claims no new foundational inequality.
